Wheat.symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery streaks on leaves running parallel to leaf veins. Severe infection causes leaf shriveling and yield loss of 30-70%.
Wheat.favorable_conditions: Cool temperature (10-15°C) with high humidity and dew. Occurs in January-March.
Wheat.spread: Wind-borne spores spread rapidly across fields
prevention: Use resistant varieties like HD-2967, PBW-550
Wheat.economic_threshold: Apply fungicide when 5% leaves show disease symptoms

Wheat.symptoms: Small green/yellow insects clustered on leaves and spikes. Causes yellowing, curling of leaves, stunted growth. Secretes honeydew causing sooty mold.
Wheat.favorable_conditions: Cool and dry weather (15-20°C). Occurs November to February.
Wheat.spread: Colonizes from field edges. Winged adults migrate from other fields.
prevention: Intercrop with mustard to attract aphid predators
organic_remedies: Neem oil @ 3 ml/litre + liquid soap 1 ml/litre
Dimethoate 30 EC 0.03% (1 ml/litre) if infestation severe
Wheat.economic_threshold: Spray when 50-100 aphids per tiller or 5-10% tillers infested

Wheat.symptoms: Plants show wilting, yellowing. Roots and stems hollow with mud tunnels. Entire plants can be pulled out easily.
Wheat.favorable_conditions: Sandy soils, dry weather, unirrigated fields
prevention: Apply FYM (Farm Yard Manure) that is well-decomposed only
Avoid stubble burning, incorporate crop residues
Deep plowing in summer to expose termite colonies
organic_remedies: Mix neem cake @ 250 kg/hectare in soil before sowing
Drench with neem oil solution around affected plants
chemical_remedies: Chlorpyrifos 20 EC @ 2.5 litre/hectare as soil drench
Imidacloprid 600 FS for seed treatment @ 7 ml/kg seed
Wheat.economic_threshold: Apply at first signs of wilting
Wheat.re_spray_interval: Apply as soil treatment before sowing

Rice.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with gray center and brown margins on leaves. Neck blast causes panicle breaking. Can cause 50-80% yield loss.
prevention: Treat seeds with Tricyclazole 75 WP @ 0.5 g/kg
Rice.economic_threshold: Spray at first lesion appearance. Must spray at panicle initiation.

Rice.symptoms: Hopperburn — plants wilt and turn brown in circular patches. Eggs laid in leaf sheaths. Mass population outbreak in humid conditions.
Rice.favorable_conditions: High humidity, dense crop canopy, excess nitrogen
Rice.spread: Winged adults migrate. Nymphs spread within field.
organic_remedies: Light trap @ 1 per hectare to monitor population
Rice.economic_threshold: 10 hoppers per hill or 1 hopper per stem
Rice.re_spray_interval: Apply only when threshold reached to preserve natural enemies

Rice.symptoms: Oval/irregular lesions with grayish-green centers on leaf sheaths. Lesions coalesce causing rotting. Yield loss 15-35%.

Tomato.symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaves, yellowing, stunted growth. Plant becomes bushy. Severe infection causes no fruit setting.
Tomato.favorable_conditions: Hot and dry weather. Whitefly population high.
Tomato.spread: Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). No direct plant-to-plant spread.
prevention: Use insect-proof net houses for nursery
Control whitefly population with yellow sticky traps
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
organic_remedies: Spray neem oil @ 3 ml/litre to control whitefly vector
Install yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 per acre
chemical_remedies: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.5 ml/litre for whitefly control
No chemical cure for virus — focus on vector control
Tomato.economic_threshold: Remove infected plants. Spray when whitefly >2 per leaf

Tomato.symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings on older leaves giving target-board appearance. Yellowing around lesions. Defoliation in severe cases.
Tomato.spread: Soil-borne, wind, rain splash, infected transplants
Tomato.economic_threshold: Spray preventively every 7-10 days during humid season

Tomato.symptoms: Larvae bore into fruits causing holes. Infested fruit rots. Entry holes visible on fruit surface. Major quality and quantity loss.
Tomato.spread: Adult moth lays eggs on flowers and young fruits
prevention: Pheromone traps @ 5 per acre for monitoring
Intercrop with marigold as trap crop

Cotton.symptoms: Pink caterpillar enters square/boll. Immature bolls fall. Seed damage inside boll. Lint quality deteriorates.
Cotton.spread: Adult moth lays eggs on squares/bolls. Caterpillar enters within 24 hours.
organic_remedies: Pheromone mass trapping (funnel trap with gossy-plure lure)
Cotton.economic_threshold: 3-5 moths per trap per night. 10% infested squares.

Cotton.symptoms: Tiny white insects on lower leaf surface. Yellowing, leaf curl, sooty mould on honeydew secretion. Also transmits Cotton Leaf Curl Virus.
Cotton.favorable_conditions: Hot and dry weather (30-40°C). Dusty conditions.
Cotton.spread: Wind dispersal. Adult migration. Dense crop favors buildup.
Cotton.economic_threshold: 10-15 adults per leaf or 15-20% plants affected
Cotton.re_spray_interval: 7-10 days. Rotate insecticides to avoid resistance.

IPM_principles: Monitor fields regularly (at least twice a week)
Record pest population and crop damage
Use economic threshold levels before spraying
Use biological controls first, then chemical as last resort
Maintain field hygiene and destroy crop residues

organic_inputs.Neem Oil: Broad spectrum insecticide/fungicide. Mix 3-5 ml/litre with liquid soap. Safe for beneficial insects when used carefully.
organic_inputs.Trichoderma: Biocontrol fungus. Controls soilborne fungal diseases. Apply 4 g/litre as soil drench.
organic_inputs.Pseudomonas fluorescens: Biocontrol bacterium. Controls bacterial and fungal diseases. Apply 5 g/litre.
organic_inputs.Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt): Biological insecticide. Controls caterpillars/borers. Apply 2 g/litre spray on eggs/larvae.
organic_inputs.NSKE 5%: Neem Seed Kernel Extract. Antifeedant and repellent. Apply 5% solution.
organic_inputs.Beauveria bassiana: Entomopathogenic fungus. Controls thrips, whitefly, aphids. Apply 5 g/litre.
